Featuring superb performances from its four-person ensemble, two of whom are physically challenged in real life, the drama provides a piercing look at the obstacles faced by disabled people and, more importantly, the human condition in general.

The play's greatest strength is its refusal to sentimentalize disability or to treat it as a source of automatic inspiration or pity.

Cost of Living is a beautiful and thrilling piece of theater about the various tendernesses of simply being human, as well as a bracing challenge to all kinds of cultural forms and genres to follow its example.
